Reviews:
	1. Name: Junaid Butt | Rating: 5
I had only one car, a Toyota, which I bought brand new by saving every single penny through honest, hard work. Unfortunately, it was stolen. Now I may never be able to buy a Toyota again because cars in Pakistan have become extremely expensive.
I cry whenever I remember my beloved car. Pakistan’s system is corrupt; I will never get my car back, nor will I be able to afford another one. Still, I love Toyota very much. My father used Toyota, and my grandfather also used Toyota. Even my son loves Toyota deeply and misses our car.
Cruel people stole it. They do not know that our car was not just a vehicle — it carried our emotions, memories, and feelings. But how would such cruel people understand human emotions, feelings, and sentiments?
My wife gives me a lot of strength and encouragement, but my heart breaks when I think about how I worked day and night, earned halal income, sacrificed my comfort, and endured hardships to buy that Toyota — and it was stolen.
That car was not just metal; it was love for me and my family. But this cruel world has no sense of compassion. It does not understand how merciless thieves have drained the colors from our lives.
We are deeply upset and extremely depressed.
